subject: Model fit evals & function-calling follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Li <sam.li@averyanalytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: model fit / tool-calling discovery

Hi Sam —

Great to meet you and the Avery team earlier. Quick recap + next steps from our side after the discovery call: 

- Goal you described: move the agent/assistant in your Insights product from rule-based extraction -> LLM-backed structured extraction with strict JSON output for downstream analytics. Must meet schema compliance and 99.99% ingestion success on high-volume nightly runs.
- Key constraints: low latency on inference for interactive QA, budget target ~ $0.0008/token, strict PII controls, SOC2 evidence required.
- What we recommended on the call: run a 2-week model-fit eval against your benchmark set (attached), focusing on Structured Output (JSON schema) and function-calling robustness (retries, non-deterministic fields). Initial model candidates: redwood-13b-quant for cost-sensitive batches and redwood-rt-large-v1 for lower-latency interactive inference.

Deliverables we'll provide by Monday:
1) A small benchmark run (5k rows) using both model candidates + our prefix-caching profile. We'll share a CSV of results per sample (attached).
2) Prompt set (v2) tailored to your schema and a short checklist for JSON schema validation and canonicalization.
3) Recommendations for function-calling: retry/backoff policy, idempotency keys, and a pre-call schema validator to catch malformed outputs before ingestion.

Can you confirm the test dataset we should use (the file you dropped in Drive was sample_v1.csv — do you want us to use that or the larger nightly export?), and whether your SRE wants us to route test traffic to the US-East Dedicated pool or your private VPC?

Thanks — next call suggested: 30-min sync next Wed to review the benchmark results and pick a rollout plan. I can set up an invite if that works.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

---
Attachments: avery-benchmarks.csv, avery-prompt-set-v2.jsonl

Thanks Marissa — great summary.

Quick answers:
- Use the nightly_export_20270620.csv (I'll upload to the Drive folder in 10 mins) — it's the closest to production.
- SRE prefers US-East Dedicated pool for latency testing; if you need private VPC for SOC2 evidence we can discuss but prefer Dedicated for the POC.

A few technical notes from our eng lead (copied inline):
> We need extra attention to two failure modes:
> 1) Schema drift: occasionally the model emits extra fields or nested arrays that our parser rejects.
> 2) Tool/fn-calls returning partial data (e.g., tool timeout) — the system must be able to retry safely without double-posting to the analytics pipeline.

Attachments: I'll attach the nightly export to the Drive and also dropped a short doc describing the JSON schema we need (schema_v3.json). Will that be sufficient?

Appreciate the benchmarks. Wed looks good for a 30-min review; suggest 11:00am ET.

—Sam
Sam Li
Senior Product Manager | Avery Analytics
sam.li@averyanalytics.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sam Li <sam.li@averyanalytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model fit / tool-calling discovery

Sam, Marissa — thanks for the notes. A couple of technical clarifications from infra/evals that will shape the run: 

1) JSON schema compliance: we'll run both a strict validator (quick fail) and a fuzz-tolerant canonicalizer (attempt to map fields and coerce types) in parallel. For the POC we'll report both "strict pass rate" and "canonicalization pass rate" to show how much post-processing is required.

2) Function-calling retries: recommended pattern for your pipeline:
   - First: synchronous function-call attempt with a 2s soft timeout for interactive flows.
   - On timeout/partial: return a deterministic error object and store the idempotency key in the retry queue.
   - Retry policy: exponential backoff (200ms initial, *2, max 5 retries) for transient tool errors.
   - If retries still fail, mark as "needs manual review" and attach the raw model output for debugging.

3) Model recommendations: start with redwood-13b-quant for nightly batch runs to meet the cost target (we expect slightly higher canonicalization work), and redwood-rt-large-v1 for interactive QA where latency/SLOs matter. If the strict pass rate for 13b-quant is <88% on the first run, we'll try redwood-20b-ptq as a fallthrough.

4) Metrics we'll produce in the CSV: sample_id, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_p50/p95, strict_schema_pass (boolean), canonicalized_pass (boolean), retry_count, error_type.

I'll start the 5k sample run on US-East Dedicated now once the nightly_export file is in the Drive and you've confirmed the dataset path.

—Rishi
Sr. ML Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
